title: Occupancy Cushion in Property Tax Refund Reviews of a Summit Reserve
content:
Where the home securing a Summit loan is no longer lived in as it was, the reserve's need in a returned property tax refund review of a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts carries a cushion. The cushion is decided from the occupancy profile (Occupancy and Residency Certification) of the reserve's Summit loan and the inspections logged on that profile.

## Rule

A month of charges is the annual property tax plus the annual hazard premium plus the annual flood premium on file, divided by twelve.

| Occupancy profile of the reserve's Summit loan | Further condition | Cushion |
|---|---|---|
| Shows non-occupancy confirmed | An occupancy inspection on that profile within the twelve months before the handling date found the home vacant or occupied by others | 2 months of charges (the vacant-home cushion) |
| Shows a health-care absence under monitoring | Its absence start date is at least 6 whole months before the handling date | 1 month of charges (the absence cushion) |
| Any other status, or neither further condition met | — | No cushion under this rule |

"Within the twelve months before the handling date" means an inspection result dated no later than the handling date and fewer than twelve whole calendar months before it. An inspection that found the home occupied by the borrower does not meet the first row; a non-occupancy confirmation with no qualifying inspection result in the window does not either.

## Boundary of the absence row (hypothetical dates, handling date 15 September)

| Absence start date | Whole months before the handling date | Cushion |
|---|---|---|
| 15 March | 6 | 1 month of charges |
| 16 March | 5 | none under this rule |

## Hypothetical figures

Annual charges on file: tax 3,000.00, hazard 1,200.00, flood 600.00. A month of charges is 4,800.00 divided by 12, 400.00. The vacant-home cushion is 800.00; the absence cushion is 400.00.
